name: FFmpeg Drawtext Timed Overlay
use_when: The agent needs simple programmatic titles, labels, debug text, or callouts directly in FFmpeg.
Text timing, position, font, size, color, shadow, border, or box styling are enough.
A lightweight overlay is safer than opening an NLE or rendering a Remotion pass.
avoid_when: The typography needs rich inline styling, responsive layout, complex masks, or spring motion.
The filter graph would require many chained text nodes that are hard to debug.
The text renderer or font availability is not controlled.

timeline_pattern.timing_rule: Use explicit start/end visibility windows rather than leaving transient labels on the full clip.
timeline_pattern.placement_rule: Use video and text dimensions to center or offset text predictably.
timeline_pattern.font_rule: Prefer explicit fontfile paths for reproducible agent renders.

motion.rule: Keep drawtext motion simple; use position, alpha, or font size expressions only when they remain readable.

keyframe_values.time_basis: Use presentation time in seconds for enable windows and expressions.
keyframe_values.center_formula: Use text width/height variables to center text and preserve centering during font-size changes.
keyframe_values.tolerance: For 30fps exports, 2 frames is about 0.067 seconds; use frame-derived times when sync matters.

sound.rule: No direct SFX rule; any text cue should follow the same frame-sync and dialogue-safety rules as other motion graphics.

captions.rule: Use drawtext for short labels or generated caption tests; use ASS or Remotion for long subtitle systems requiring richer layout.

color.rule: Use shadow, border, or a backing box only when needed for contrast; avoid heavy styling that makes letters muddy.

implementation.ffmpeg: Create a drawtext filter with explicit text, fontfile, fontsize, fontcolor, x/y placement, and enable timing; chain labeled streams only while the graph stays debuggable.
implementation.remotion: Represent the same overlay as a text component with startFrame/endFrame, safeRegion, and style tokens when richer animation is needed.
implementation.blender: Use text objects for spatial labels, then render or composite over the timeline.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Trim a text layer to the intended range and set font, size, color, shadow, and position manually.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use Essential Graphics text with explicit in/out trims and guides for safe placement.

common_mistakes: Relying on system font lookup when the render environment may not have that font.
Forgetting to escape text or expression punctuation in generated filter strings.
Leaving a text overlay enabled longer than the spoken concept.
Using heavy outline/box styling as decoration instead of contrast support.
Testing placement only on one frame while footage contrast changes.
qc: Fontfile resolves in the render environment.
Text appears and clears within the intended time window.
Text is readable on representative bright, dark, and busy frames.
Generated filter graph is logged or reproducible from structured data.
Text avoids faces, proof, UI, products, maps, captions, and action.
